# Glossary

<!-- Generated from canon by scripts/build_derived.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Theme | A costume layer of palette, type, motion grammar, transitions and video language, identified by a TX number and a codename. |
| Codename | The only public name a theme has. No franchise names, ever. |
| Card | The eleven-field record that defines a theme. |
| Register | Creative, editorial or B2B: who the property is for. It sets the intensity. |
| Boardroom translation | The one-line B2B version of a theme. |
| Swap test | The homage check: swap the theme for its genre neighbor and cut anything that only makes sense as one property. |
| Data shape | The dominant shape of a story's data: flow, network, comparison, timeline, terrain, score or document. |
| Beat | One timed section of a reel loop. Each beat demonstrates one web slot. |
| Manifest | The record that ships with a build, including the theme line. |
| Ledger | The running list of shipped builds, used to keep themes from repeating. |
| S1 | Hero signature: The opening moment that only this subject could have. The theme dresses it; the subject still decides it. |
| S2 | Section transitions: How one chapter hands off to the next: wipes, rolls, cuts, decodes. |
| S3 | Ambient layer: The texture that runs under everything: grain, scanlines, haze, drifting particles. Always quiet, always pausable. |
| S4 | Data skin: How charts, numbers and labels look and move. Every data beat in the reel demonstrates one. |
| S5 | Interaction and focus: Hover, focus and press states, including the page's one call to action. |
| T1 | CSS and SVG: Transforms, gradients, clip paths and SVG strokes. The default tier and the safest. |
| T2 | Canvas and script: 2D canvas, particles and animation libraries. Needs a pause control when it runs past five seconds. |
| T3 | WebGL: Shaders and 3D. At most one WebGL layer per page, and never fluid simulation in B2B work. |
| D, I | Phase 1: decide format and modules. A theme never picks the format. |
| U1 | Essence extraction: five words and the dominant data shape. |
| U2 | Concept triptych: three directions, at most one theme-led. |
| U3 | Ledger check against recent builds. |
| R | Register and look: intensity, palette, type. |
| E | Effects: fill the five slots. |
| C | Code: tokens, fonts and the build. |
| T | Tests: homage swap test, safety and accessibility. |
| M | Manifest: the record that ships with the build. |
